correctness.rationale: For every outside a_i and b_i the proof derives exact neighbor-count formulas q-1_{i in J} and p-1_{i in I}. Constancy forces either I=J or I union J=[n] unless one side is full; the cross-side equality in the union-full case forces |I|=|J|. The converse and positivity are checked case by case. Counting the three disjoint structural families yields the polynomial, the degree-two minimum layer, and the central-trinomial total. A standalone exhaustive checker independently confirms the literal definition, classification, coefficients, minima, totals for 3<=n<=9 and the complement equivalence for 3<=n<=8. The finite computation is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification for a classical graph family obtained by deleting one perfect matching from K_{n,n}, exactly the perturbation that makes fair domination index-sensitive. It refines the unchanged scalar minimum into the full polynomial, shows the minimum-set count collapses from n^2 to n, and identifies the total count with a central-trinomial expression. These are structural consequences useful for comparison, enumeration, and complement formulations, not a routine parameter substitution.
